testSupportsTemplate?: string - These options are wired into behavior: - ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate }) is called for all test files, handling insertion of missing file-level @supports templates. - buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?: string): - Constructs a default baseTemplate: "@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ" when no custom template is provided. - Wraps it into a multi-line JSDoc with an explicit TODO line: /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ - This matches the story’s template examples and satisfies: - REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE (auto-add @supports template when missing), - REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER (clear placeholder line), - REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE (no attempt to infer real story/REQs). - insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?): - Detects and preserves a shebang line by inserting the template after it, otherwise at file start. - Uses fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([insertIndex, insertIndex], templateComment), touching only comments. - Satisfies REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE and REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE for file-level templates (no code changes, only added comment block). - ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions): - Scans all comments for any @supports; if one is found, it does nothing (avoids duplicate templates). - If no @supports is found, reports messageId: "missingFileSupports". - Provides a fixer only when autoFixOptions.autoFixTestTemplate !== false, calling insertSupportsTemplate with optional testSupportsTemplate override. - JSDoc includes: - @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.,Helper implementation – src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts (REQ prefix normalization): - normalizeReqId(raw: string): - Trims and converts to uppercase; early-exits if value doesn’t start with "REQ" to avoid inventing IDs. - After the REQ prefix, strips leading separators, converts whitespace/underscores to hyphens, and collapses multiple hyphens. - Returns a canonical REQ-... string based on the existing identifier, fulfilling REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE. - normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description: string): - If the string already matches canonical /^\[REQ-[^\]]+]/, returns null (no fix), preserving already-correct test names (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE). - Handles malformed prefixes at the beginning of the description exactly as specified in the story: - Spacing: "[ REQ-XXX ] ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ...". - Underscore: "[REQ_XXX] ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ...". - Parentheses: "(REQ-XXX) ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ...". - Lowercase: "[req-xxx] ..." → "[REQ-XXX] ...". - Only returns a new string when a REQ-like token is present at the start; otherwise returns null, ensuring no fabricated prefixes (REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode): - Reads the raw literal text and preserves the original quote type (' / " / `) while escaping backslashes and embedded quotes appropriately. - Falls back to JSON.stringify when the raw form is unknown. - This keeps code structure and formatting intact while only changing the string content, implementing REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE. - handleItOrTestCall(context, node, description, options): - Respects requireTestReqPrefix; if false, it does nothing. - If description does not begin with a canonical [REQ-...] pattern: - If autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, computes normalizedDescription via normalizeReqPrefixInDescription. - Always reports messageId: "missingReqPrefix" for validation (Story 020.0 behavior). - Only attaches a fixer when: - autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false, - normalizedDescription !== null (i.e., there was a recognizable REQ ID to normalize), - first argument is a string Literal. - The fixer uses createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw to replace only the literal, leaving the rest of the test code unchanged. - This satisfies: - REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT: malformed-but-identifiable prefixes are corrected. - REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE: no fix is applied when there is no recognizable REQ ID. - REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE: only the test name string is changed. - REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE: missing prefixes are reported but never auto-generated.,Visitor wiring – src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts: - For describe, delegates to handleDescribeCall, which only validates the description against a regex and does not add or infer story references, staying within the "explicitly OUT OF SCOPE" section of this story. - For it/test, delegates to handleItOrTestCall where the malformed-prefix normalization and safe auto-fix live. - JSDoc on handleCallExpression includes @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE, ensuring traceability to this story.,Tests – tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts (explicit coverage for Story 021.0): - traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for Story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX are fully implemented and verified: - File-level @supports templates with clear TODO placeholders are auto-inserted only when missing and only for test files. - Malformed [REQ-XXX] prefixes in it/test names are safely normalized (spacing, delimiters, parentheses, casing) without inventing new IDs. - Auto-fixes operate only on annotations and string literals, preserving test behavior and formatting, and are gated so they apply only when safe. - The feature integrates with ESLint’s --fix workflow through meta.fixable: "code" and is thoroughly covered by dedicated tests that all pass. - User-facing API documentation accurately describes the new auto-fix capabilities and configuration options. Therefore this story’s implementation status is PASSED.
